CHAPTER 4.2 · LEARNING AREA 4

CHAPTER 4.2 · LEARNING AREA 4 · FEBRUARY · MARCH

Solids and frustums

A bucket, a flowerpot, a lampshade, a concrete base: many things are cones or pyramids whose top is missing. You will revise the prism, cylinder, pyramid, cone and sphere, derive the formulae for the frustum of a pyramid and of a cone and calculate the mass and cost of workpieces.

8 LESSONS2 UNITSVOLUMEWORKPIECES
WHAT YOU WILL LEARN IN THIS CHAPTER
  • calculate the volume and surface area of the familiar solids confidently
  • calculate composite solids by the principle of decomposition
  • derive and apply the formulae for the frustum of a pyramid and of a cone
  • find the mass from the volume and the density, as well as production costs and profit

UNIT 14 LESSONS

1Representing and calculating solids

The cone fits into the cylinder exactly three times. For all pointed solids: the volume is a third of the base area times the height. You split composite solids into familiar parts, calculate each part and add or subtract.

KEY POINT · VOLUME AND SURFACE AREA

Prism, cylinder: $V = G \cdot h$; cylinder $V = \pi r^2 h$, curved surface $M = 2\pi r h$.

Pyramid, cone: $V = \tfrac13 G \cdot h$; cone $V = \tfrac13 \pi r^2 h$, curved surface $M = \pi r s$ with the slant height $s = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2}$.

Sphere: $V = \tfrac43 \pi r^3$, $S = 4 \pi r^2$.

Mass $m = V \cdot \rho$ (density). Units: $1\,\text{l} = 1\,\text{dm}^3 = 1000\,\text{cm}^3$.

Radius or diameter? The formulae need the radius. With the diameter, the sphere becomes eight times too large.

Densities: wood about $0.6$, concrete about $2.4$, steel about $7.85\,\tfrac{\text{g}}{\text{cm}^3}$.

INTERACTIVE · PYRAMID AND CONE

Pointed solids compared: base area, height, curved surface and volume.

EXAMPLE 1 · COMPOSITE

On top of a cube with an edge of 6 cm sits a pyramid with the same base and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the volume.

$216 + \tfrac13 \cdot 36 \cdot 4 = 216 + 48 =$ 264 cm³

EXAMPLE 2 · THE PIPE

A steel pipe is 10 cm long, with an outer radius of 5 cm and an inner radius of 3 cm. How heavy is it?

$V = \pi (25 - 9) \cdot 10 = 160\pi \approx 502.7\,\text{cm}^3$, $m \approx 502.7 \cdot 7.85 \approx$ 3946 g, just under 4 kg.

EXERCISES

Calculate the volume and the curved surface of a cylinder with $r = 3$ cm and $h = 10$ cm.

$V = 90\pi \approx 282.7\,\text{cm}^3$, $M = 60\pi \approx 188.5\,\text{cm}^2$.

A sphere has a diameter of 12 cm. Calculate its volume and surface area.

$r = 6$ cm: $V = 288\pi \approx 904.8\,\text{cm}^3$, $S = 144\pi \approx 452.4\,\text{cm}^2$.

A square pyramid has a base edge of 6 cm and a slant height of 5 cm (height of a side face). Calculate its perpendicular height, surface area and volume.

$h = \sqrt{25 - 9} = 4$ cm, $S = 36 + 4 \cdot 15 = 96\,\text{cm}^2$, $V = \tfrac13 \cdot 36 \cdot 4 = 48\,\text{cm}^3$.

A tin is to hold exactly 1 l and has a radius of 5 cm. How tall must it be?

$h = \tfrac{1000}{25\pi} \approx 12.7$ cm

The inside of an aquarium measures 80 cm × 40 cm × 50 cm. It is filled to 90%. How many litres is that, and how heavy is the water ($1\,\text{l} \approx 1\,\text{kg}$)?

$160\,\text{l} \cdot 0.9 = 144\,\text{l}$, so about 144 kg.

UNIT 24 LESSONS

2Frustum of a pyramid and frustum of a cone

The bucket is a cone whose tip has been cut off. So its volume is that of the whole cone minus that of the small tip. If you work this out in general, you get a formula in which only the two radii and the height of the frustum appear.

KEY POINT · FRUSTUM

Frustum of a cone with the radii $R$, $r$ and the height $h$: $V = \dfrac{\pi h}{3}\,(R^2 + R r + r^2)$, curved surface $M = \pi s (R + r)$ with $s = \sqrt{h^2 + (R - r)^2}$.

Frustum of a pyramid with the areas $G_1$, $G_2$: $V = \dfrac{h}{3}\,\bigl(G_1 + \sqrt{G_1 G_2} + G_2\bigr)$.

Check with limiting cases: $r = 0$ gives the cone, $r = R$ the cylinder.

Half the height: if you cut a cone off at half its height, the tip has only $\left(\tfrac12\right)^3 = \tfrac18$ of the volume. $\tfrac78$ remains in the frustum.

INTERACTIVE · FRUSTUM OF A CONE AND OF A PYRAMID

Change the radii or edges and the height. The tool calculates the volume with the formula and as the difference of two whole solids – and the mass for the chosen material.

EXAMPLE 3 · THE BUCKET

A bucket has a radius of 15 cm at the top and 12 cm at the bottom and is 30 cm high. How many litres does it hold?

$V = \tfrac{30\pi}{3}(225 + 180 + 144) = 5490\pi \approx 17{,}247\,\text{cm}^3 \approx$ 17.2 l

EXAMPLE 4 · THE CONCRETE BASE

A base is a frustum of a pyramid with square faces (edges 1 m and 0.6 m) and is 0.5 m high. Concrete weighs $2.4\,\tfrac{\text{t}}{\text{m}^3}$ and costs €150 per m³.

$V = \tfrac{0.5}{3}(1 + 0.6 + 0.36) \approx 0.327\,\text{m}^3$, mass ≈ 784 kg, cost of the concrete ≈ €49.

EXERCISES

A frustum of a cone has $R = 4$ cm, $r = 2$ cm and $h = 6$ cm. Calculate its volume.

$2\pi \cdot 28 = 56\pi \approx 175.9\,\text{cm}^3$

A frustum of a pyramid has square faces with edges of 4 cm and 2 cm and is 3 cm high. Calculate its volume.

$\tfrac33 (16 + 8 + 4) = 28\,\text{cm}^3$

A lampshade is the curved surface of a frustum of a cone with $R = 20$ cm, $r = 10$ cm and a height of 24 cm. How much fabric do you need?

$s = \sqrt{576 + 100} = 26$ cm, $M = \pi \cdot 26 \cdot 30 = 780\pi \approx 2450.4\,\text{cm}^2$.

A pyramid ($a = 6$ cm, $h = 8$ cm) is cut off at half its height. Calculate the volume of the frustum as a difference and with the formula.

$96 - 12 = 84\,\text{cm}^3$. Formula: $\tfrac43 (36 + 18 + 9) = 84\,\text{cm}^3$.

A workpiece costs €12 for material and €8 for labour and is sold for €32. What percentage of the costs is the profit, what percentage of the selling price?

Profit €12: 60% of the costs, 37.5% of the selling price.

REVIEW · DEEPEN · CONNECT

A cone has $r = 6$ cm and $h = 10$ cm. Calculate its volume.

$120\pi \approx 377.0\,\text{cm}^3$

A flowerpot has a radius of 10 cm at the top and 7 cm at the bottom and is 12 cm high. How much soil fits into it?

$4\pi \cdot 219 = 876\pi \approx 2752\,\text{cm}^3 \approx 2.75$ l

A frustum of a pyramid has square faces with edges of 10 cm and 4 cm, the trapezium faces are 5 cm high. How high is the frustum?

Overhang $3$ cm, $h = \sqrt{25 - 9} = 4$ cm.

Connecting: for advertising, a model of a bucket is built at the scale 1 : 2. How much volume does the model have compared with the original, how much material for the curved surface?

Volume $\left(\tfrac12\right)^3 = \tfrac18$, curved surface $\left(\tfrac12\right)^2 = \tfrac14$.

EXCURSIONHISTORY

A frustum of a pyramid almost 4000 years ago

The Moscow Mathematical Papyrus comes from ancient Egypt, around 1850 BC. In problem 14 the volume of a frustum of a pyramid is calculated: height 6, edge 4 at the bottom, edge 2 at the top. The scribe calculates $4^2 + 4 \cdot 2 + 2^2 = 28$ and multiplies it by a third of the height: 56.

That is exactly our formula $V = \tfrac{h}{3}\bigl(G_1 + \sqrt{G_1 G_2} + G_2\bigr)$. How the Egyptians found it is still not known exactly today.

Source: Moscow Mathematical Papyrus, problem 14 (Pushkin Museum, Moscow); after V. J. Katz: A History of Mathematics, 3rd ed. 2009, ch. 1.
